title: Empires of Yesterday — Data Dictionary
subtitle: Guidance on the tables that populate the game. Unity Catalog–style reference: pick a table to see its grain, source, and columns.

catalogs.name: Two Worlds — Campaign (authority tables)
catalogs.description: Narrow, normalized authority tables for the turn-based Two Worlds mode. These hold sim truth; wide-row reports (see Battle replay / presentation) are derived projections. Source crate: rust/eon_engine.

tables.name: province
tables.grain: One row per province (a large carved region of the globe).
tables.description: A campaign region. Ownership is derived from the dominion (faith) tide, not stored directly.

columns.name: is_land
columns.desc: Land provinces participate in the tide; water blocks it.

columns.name: elevation
columns.desc: Terrain height. Ignored by dominion diffusion (height-independent tide); affects battle terrain/movement.

columns.name: neighbors
columns.desc: Adjacency (borders + sea lanes) used by the tide and army movement.

columns.name: dom
columns.desc: Dominion/faith mass held by each faction here. The visible tide; drives owner().

columns.name: unrest
columns.desc: Corruption pressure from enemy faith in an owned province; high unrest erodes the owner's faith.

columns.name: temple_owner
columns.desc: Faction whose temple sits here (a fixed dominion amplifier). Null if none.

columns.name: capital_of
columns.desc: Faction whose capital sits here (strongest fixed source). Null if none.

columns.name: has_throne
columns.desc: Throne of Ascension marker for the ascension win condition.

columns.name: deposit
columns.desc: Gem deposit (Aurelium/Verdantite/Emberstone) credited to the owner. Null if none.

tables.notes: owner() = strict-max dominion above a threshold, else neutral. Diffusion conserves per-faction mass; injection/cancellation post to the ledger.

tables.name: faction
tables.grain: One row per faction (player or AI).
tables.description: A competing power (e.g. Azure, Crimson).

columns.name: is_ai
columns.desc: Driven by the built-in AI (both sides can be AI for AI-vs-AI).

columns.name: alive
columns.desc: Still in the game (has faith or armies).

columns.name: ascension_points
columns.desc: Owned thrones this turn; drives the Ascension victory.

tables.name: army
tables.grain: One row per army (commander stack) on the campaign map.
tables.description: A movable force of squads, rendered on the globe as a commander billboard; expands into individual units in battle.

columns.name: move_to
columns.desc: Movement order for the turn; resolved in the Movement phase.

tables.notes: Two enemy armies meeting in a province trigger a battle (resolved by the battle engine).

tables.name: squad
tables.grain: One row per regiment within an army.
tables.description: A block of identical units. Expands to `count` individual soldiers/bombers in battle.

columns.name: kind
columns.desc: Unit type. Soldiers have Verdantite upkeep; bombers have none (A14).

tables.notes: Per-kind stats (hp, attack, reach, speed) live on UnitKind in model.rs.

tables.name: agent
tables.grain: One row per agent (meta-game character).
tables.description: A Total-War-style operative acting on the campaign each turn.

columns.name: kind
columns.desc: Verb: amplify faith / sap enemy faith / kill agents / diplomacy / reveal.

columns.name: alive
columns.desc: Killed agents are removed from play.

tables.notes: Prophets/priests amplify dominion from their location during the Dominion phase.

catalogs.name: Two Worlds — Accounting (transaction ledger)
catalogs.description: The engine is a double-entry ledger: narrow ordered transactions are journal entries; wide-row reports are the finished statements. Every state change is a balanced posting so the books always tie out (trial_balance == 0). Source: rust/eon_engine/src/ledger.rs.

tables.name: ledger_txn
tables.grain: One row per posted transaction (append-only journal).
tables.description: Immutable journal entry. Corrections are reversing transactions, never edits.

columns.name: phase
columns.desc: Order-of-operations phase: income, upkeep, agents, rituals, movement, battles, dominion, corruption, events, win_check.

columns.name: kind
columns.desc: Stable op tag, e.g. inject_capital, cancel, casualties, consecrate, spy_sap.

tables.notes: The journal digest proves replay determinism. Diffusion conserves mass, so it posts nothing; only mint/destroy/transfer post.

tables.name: account_balance
tables.grain: One row per tracked account (running balance).
tables.description: Conserved quantities. Wide-row reports must reconcile against these aggregates (trial balance).

columns.name: account
columns.desc: Dominion(f) / DominionSource(f) / DominionSink / UnitsAlive(f) / UnitSource(f) / Casualties(f) / Gems(f,path) / GemSource(f).

columns.name: balance
columns.desc: Running total; sum of all balances is always ~0 (double-entry).

tables.notes: Example invariants: sum_provinces(dom[f]) == Dominion(f); UnitsAlive(f) + Casualties(f) == recruited(f).

catalogs.name: Two Worlds — Battle (baked replay)
catalogs.description: Battles are resolved once (deterministically, spatial-hash O(n)) and baked to wide-row frames the HD-2D viewer interpolates at ~60fps. Source: rust/eon_engine/src/battle.rs.

tables.name: battle_report
tables.grain: One row per resolved battle.
tables.description: Outcome + baked frames for a battle in a contested province.

columns.name: winner
columns.desc: Winning faction, or null on a draw.

columns.name: ticks
columns.desc: Sim ticks the battle ran (up to MAX_TICKS).

columns.name: frames
columns.desc: Recorded every RECORD_STRIDE ticks; the replay track.

tables.notes: Casualties post back to the World ledger; the victor consecrates the province (a balanced dominion injection).

tables.name: battle_frame
tables.grain: One row per recorded tick of a battle.
tables.description: A snapshot of all units at a tick. Unit index is stable across frames, enabling interpolation.

columns.name: units
columns.desc: All units, in stable order (see unit_snapshot).

tables.notes: Streamed to Godot via get_last_battle_frame_xy(index, frame); meta (fac/kind) fetched once via get_last_battle_meta.

tables.name: unit_snapshot
tables.grain: One row per unit per frame.
tables.description: A single unit's position/state at a frame (billboard sprite in the viewer).
tables.notes: The viewer buckets units by (faction, kind) into MultiMesh draw calls for scale.

tables.name: locomotor
tables.grain: One row per UnitKind.
tables.description: How a Compact kind moves on the battle slab. Static Rust table; not JSON.

columns.name: blocked_by_hill / blocked_by_ruin
columns.desc: Land walks around; air flies over.

columns.name: ford_ok
columns.desc: River is a ford, not a wall.

tables.name: nav_policy
tables.grain: One row per (situation, attack_style).
tables.description: Join situation → intent. ST_IDLE is only legal for TrainHold.

columns.name: situation
columns.desc: Routing / Train / DriveBy / HaltInReach / Advance / AaClose / AirIgnore / FollowLane.

columns.name: intent
columns.desc: FollowGuide / CloseContact / HaltAim / Overfly / RoutHome / TrainHold.

tables.notes: Guides and land bodies steer around nav_blocker rows (hill, ruin). No per-body A*.

tables.name: nav_blocker
tables.grain: One row per solid occupancy on the slab (hill, ruin).
tables.description: Static circles land steers around. Air ignores land blockers. Rust tables, not JSON.

columns.name: cx / cy / r
columns.desc: Circle in slab space. Nav radius is occupancy plus a walk-around pad.

catalogs.name: Two Worlds — Config (tunables)
catalogs.description: Global sim knobs for the campaign + battle pacing. Source: rust/eon_engine/src/model.rs :: Config.

tables.name: config
tables.grain: Singleton (one row).
tables.description: Balance constants; product law lives in DESIGN.md § Design locks.

columns.name: thrones_to_win
columns.desc: Thrones needed for Ascension (set very high in globe mode to force a contest).

columns.name: turn_limit
columns.desc: Hard cap; leader by land then dominion wins by Score.

columns.name: dominion_alive_eps
columns.desc: Faith below this counts as eliminated (dominion-kill win).

tables.notes: Battle-side constants (BATTLE_WIDTH/HEIGHT, MAX_TICKS, RECORD_STRIDE, GRID_CELL) live in battle.rs. Shot cadence is KindProfile attack_interval (ticks); air keeps BOMB_COOLDOWN as a floor.

catalogs.name: Live World Conquest — SCD1 domains
catalogs.description: The shipping real-time game's live authority is the Rust WorldDataset; Godot presentation is apply-only via SCD1 per-domain versioned pulls. Source: DESIGN.md, RUST.md, Scd1DomainPull.gd, rust/empire_territory/src/domain_version.rs.

tables.name: territory
tables.grain: One row per grid cell (per-domain versioned).
tables.description: Owners + pressure per cell; the fluid conquest truth.

columns.name: cell
columns.desc: Grid cell index (equirect or sphere cell).

columns.name: version
columns.desc: SCD1 row version; Godot pulls rows with version > last.

tables.notes: Owner = simple majority pressure. Godot never authors this in live Play.

tables.name: structures
tables.grain: One row per structure (SCD1 versioned).
tables.description: Outposts, barracks, hangars (corridor kept for save/compat).

columns.name: version
columns.desc: SCD1 row version; removed_ids carry tombstones.

tables.notes: See structure_record_to_dict in ffi_convert.rs for the full field set.

tables.name: agents (soldiers)
tables.grain: One row per living soldier (SCD1 versioned).
tables.description: Ground units with aura + erode; Aurelium+Verdantite upkeep.
tables.notes: Caps: 5 per barracks, 100 global (Design lock F6). Ferry on open water at 0.25x (R2).

tables.name: bombers
tables.grain: One row per living bomber (SCD1 versioned).
tables.description: Air units; bomb any non-team land; no continuous upkeep (A14).

tables.name: wallet
tables.grain: One row per team resource wallet (SCD1 versioned).
tables.description: Supply + minerals (Aurelium/Verdantite/Emberstone) authority.
tables.notes: Income/spend applied in Rust (apply_resource_tick_delta), then mirrored to Godot.

catalogs.name: Content / Reference
catalogs.description: Static content and constants that parameterize both modes.

tables.name: economy_catalog
tables.grain: One row per structure/unit kind.
tables.description: Costs, drains, caps for structures and units.

columns.name: upkeep
columns.desc: Continuous upkeep (soldiers only; bombers none — A14).

tables.notes: Rust economy.rs mirrors these for parity; QA checks catalog vs config.

tables.name: world_conquest_config
tables.grain: Singleton reference of live-game constants.
tables.description: Pacing, camera, globe, and flow constants for the live World Conquest game.
tables.notes: Numbers are code-truth; DESIGN.md explains the why.
